title: Drama: Pressure
body:
EPISODE PACKAGE
====

EPISODE TITLE: THE SINKING HANDCART
SUBJECT / TOPIC: INTEGRATED SCIENCE / Pressure
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
AGE RATING: 10+ (student-safe)
DURATION: 8 minutes
VISUAL STYLE: naturalistic live-action look with clear prop inserts (or 2D/3D cartoon adaptation of the same blocking)

LEARNING TIE-IN: Free the cart without breaking goods or injuring backs

LOGLINE: A handcart sticks in mud until the movers change contact area and rediscover pressure as force over area.

WORLD & CAST

• Setting / era: EXT. muddy estate road after rain
• BARAKA: delivery helper, strong, impatient. Costume: boots, overalls.
• IDRIS: physics-minded friend. Costume: raincoat.
• BIBI FATUMA: customer waiting for goods. Costume: lesso, umbrella.

SCREENPLAY

SCENE 1 — EXT./INT. OPENING LOCATION — DAY

ACTION: BARAKA enters the world of the story with a clear goal: Free the cart without breaking goods or injuring backs. Camera follows hands and faces, not a chalkboard.

BARAKA
If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.

IDRIS
Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Wide establishing → medium two-shot. Ambient authentic location SFX. Soft hopeful underscore.

SCENE 2 — SAME / NEARBY — DAY

ACTION: Obstacle appears. Stakes rise. Props related to the science idea are handled as real objects, not lecture aids.

BARAKA
It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.

BIBI FATUMA
If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Close-ups on props and worried eyes. Tension riser.

BARAKA
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

IDRIS
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 3 — CONFRONTATION — DAY

ACTION: WRONG WAY: Baraka pushes harder on a narrow plank, sinking deeper. The problem worsens. Meaning stays in action and argument — characters never read notes aloud.

BARAKA
See? I did what everyone does.

IDRIS
And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Handheld urgency. Cut to the failed result.

SCENE 4 — DISCOVERY — DAY/NIGHT

ACTION: A clue appears through action — a label, a measurement, a safer method, a remembered rule spoken as dialogue while doing.

IDRIS
Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.

BARAKA
Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Insert shots of evidence. Music shifts from tension to curiosity.

BARAKA
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

IDRIS
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 5 — SECOND ATTEMPT — DAY

ACTION: RIGHT WAY: Idris widens the base with boards; pressure drops; cart moves. Characters perform the corrected action step by step.

BARAKA
This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.

BIBI FATUMA
I can see the difference already.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Cleaner framed shots; success micro-beats.

SCENE 6 — COMPLICATION — DAY

ACTION: A new obstacle or time pressure forces them to apply the idea again, proving it was not luck.

BIBI FATUMA
We are not done. Another problem just arrived.

IDRIS
Same science. Fresh situation. Go.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Parallel cut or ticking clock motif without graphic peril.

BARAKA
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

IDRIS
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 7 — RESOLUTION — DAY

ACTION: Payoff: goal achieved. Characters show the result; still no voice-over lecture.

BARAKA
It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.

IDRIS
Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Warm wider shot; relieved faces; result hero insert.

SCENE 8 — BUTTON — DAY

ACTION: Final acted beat tying emotion to the learning without reading notes aloud.

BIBI FATUMA
Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.

BARAKA
And we will check the evidence first.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Slow push-in; music resolves.

BARAKA
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

IDRIS
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

BOOKENDS

• COLD OPEN (max 10s): Quick hook image of the failed first attempt — then cut to title THE SINKING HANDCART.
• CLOSING REFLECTION CARD (max 10s): On-screen question — How does increasing area change pressure for the same force? Answer must match lesson solutions (P = F / A; larger A → smaller P).

CAPTIONS

BARAKA: If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.
IDRIS: Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.
BARAKA: It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.
BIBI FATUMA: If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.
BARAKA: See? I did what everyone does.
IDRIS: And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.
IDRIS: Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.
BARAKA: Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.
BARAKA: This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.
BIBI FATUMA: I can see the difference already.
BIBI FATUMA: We are not done. Another problem just arrived.
IDRIS: Same science. Fresh situation. Go.
BARAKA: It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.
IDRIS: Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.
BIBI FATUMA: Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.
BARAKA: And we will check the evidence first.

ASSET LIST

• Characters: BARAKA, IDRIS, BIBI FATUMA
• Costumes: as listed above
• Locations: EXT. muddy estate road after rain
• Props: topic-authentic objects for Pressure
• Key shots: failed attempt insert, evidence insert, successful payoff insert

Study pages available for fidelity: 20
DRAMA NOTE: No voice-over of lesson notes. Meaning travels through action and in-character dialogue.

DISPLAY-CLEAN: PASS | fixes: headings=0 bold=0 tables=0 code=0 formulas=0

sources.subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
sources.excerpt: 3.2 Pressure I. Meaning of pressure. Pressure is defined as the force acting normally per unit area. Normally here means at a right angle or perpendicularly.
